plan: With 3 bidders and uniform value distribution on [0,49], the standard first-price auction Nash equilibrium strategy is to bid (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for 3 bidders. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $31, so optimal bid ≈ $20.67. This shades my bid appropriately below value to maximize expected profit while maintaining competitive winning chances against Betty and Charles.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which for n=3 bidders is 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $22, so I'll bid approximately $14.7, which maximizes expected profit given the equilibrium strategy assuming other bidders behave similarly rationally.

With value $40 and 3 bidders (n=3) drawing uniformly from $0-49, the optimal first-price auction bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3 of my value, assuming others bid similarly rationally. This balances winning probability against profit margin. Bidding too close to $40 leaves little profit if I win; bidding too low risks losing to others with similar shading. I'll bid approximately $26.7 to maximize expected profit.
